questions.question: A shop keeper sold two articles. He sold one article at Rs. 29,337 and got 27% profit. He sold the other article at Rs. 14,206.50 and got 23% loss. what is his overall gain or loss per cent (correct to nearest integer)?

CP = SPover (100+G) × 100,

CP = Cost Price

SP = Selling Price

G = Gain %

Cost price for Article 1 = 29,337over 127 × 100 = Rs 23,100

Cost Price for Article 2 = 14,206.50over 77 × 100 = Rs 18,450

Total cost price for Artcle 1 and Article 2 = Rs 23,100 + Rs 18,450 = Rs 41,550

Total selling price for Artcle 1 and Article 2 = Rs 29,337 + Rs 14,206.50 = Rs 43,543.50

Gain = Rs 43,543.50 - Rs 41,550 = Rs 1993.50

Gain % = 1993.50over 41,550 × 100 = 5% (approximated to the nearest integer).

∴ **The net gain on the transaction is 5%.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a work in 16 days. If A alone can do the same work in 48 days, then in how many days can B alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
Given data:

Time taken by A and B to complete the work = 16 days

Time taken by A to complete the work = 48 days

Calculations:

Work done by A in 1 day = 1over 48

Work done by A and B in 1 day = 1over 16

Total work done by B in 1 day = 1over 16 - 1over 48 = 3-1over 48 = 1over 24

Time taken by B to complete total work individually = 24 days.

∴ B completes the total work in 24 days.

questions.question: P, Q and R participated in a cycle race of 4000 metres. P cycles twice as fast as Q and R cycles 1over2 as fast as Q. If R completes the race in 40 minutes, then what is the speed (in km/h) of P?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

S = D over T, where

D = Distance

S = Speed

T = Time 

**Concept:**

Speed and Time are inversely proportional. This means that if the speed is more, time required will be less and vice-versa.

**Calculation:**

According to the question-

R cycles 1over2 as fast as Q and requires 40 minutes to complete the race

⇒ Q requires 20 min to complete the race.

P cycles twice as fast as Q

⇒ P requires 10 min i.e., half as much timing as Q.

Total time taken by P in seconds = 10 × 60 = 600 sec

Speed of P = 4000over 600 = 20over3 m/s

Speed of P in km/h = 20over3 × 18over5 = 24 km/h

∴ **The speed of P is 24 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** To convert m/s into km/h, we multiply by 18over5 . Conversely, to convert km/h to m/s, we multiply by 5over18.

questions.question: In a test consisting of 80 questions, Anita answered 60% of the first 55 questions correctly. What per cent of the remaining questions should she answer correctly to obtain 70% in the entire exam?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total question to be answered correctly = 70over100 × 80 = 56

Questions already answered correctly = 60over100 × 55 = 33

Remaining number of questions to be answered correctly = 56 - 33 = 23

Remaining questions available = 80 - 55 = 25

Required percentage = 23over 25 × 100 = 92%

∴ **Anita should answer 92% of the remaining questions correctly.**

questions.question: On a certain sum, simple interest for 2 years is Rs. 9,600 whereas the compound interest compounded annually is Rs. 10,176. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Formula:

P = SI×100over R× T

A = P × (1 + Rover 100)T

CI = A - P

where-

A = Amount from Compound Interest

P = Principal

SI = Simple Interest

R = Rate

T = Time

CI = Compound Interest

**Concept:**

Compound interest includes interest calculated on the interest portion for the subsequent period. Hence, the compound interest for the 2nd year is the interest calculated on the interest for the 1st year along with the interest for the 2nd year. 

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Interest calculated on the interest part for the 1st year.

**Calculation:**

SI for one year = 9600 ÷ 2 = Rs 4800

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Rs 10,176 - Rs 9600 = Rs 576

Rate of Interest = 576over 4800 × 100 = 12%

**∴ Rate of interest is 12 p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

CI and SI for the 1st year are the same. Compound Interest comes into play from the second year provided interest is calculated annually.
